notes: Context: SMB productivity app that auto-summarizes meeting notes and routes to workflows. Mostly self-serve on hosted API.
Primary problem: streaming + json-mode + function-calling -> downstream parser frequently throws JSONDecodeError when chunks arrive mid-object.
Customer quote: "The assistant uses function_call for 'create_task' but our parser fails intermittently when stream breaks parts of the function args."
- Delta sequence sometimes yields partial 'function_call' object in one delta and remainder in next -> invalid JSON when trying to parse chunk-by-chunk.
- Sometimes 'name' in function_call is 'create_task' but schema expects 'task_create' (naming mismatch on their side).
Conversation notes: customer uses Node SDK; their code tries to JSON.parse on each chunk rather than assembling full message; wants best practices and examples.
Customer tried workaround: buffer until 'finish_reason' === 'function_call' but finish_reason appears only on last delta; still saw race conditions.
SE notes: suggest using per-message assembly strategy + validate against function schema before invoking internal tool; provide sample helper util to merge deltas safely.
Risk: SMB is time-sensitive; if unresolved, customer may switch to competitor with clearer streaming examples.
Ask: Provide patched example in Node + Python SDK showing streaming assembly, function schema validation (strict), and fallback non-streaming call pattern.
Suggested demo: 30m session to walk through code, reproduce, push a docs PR to SDK examples repository, and share a quick fix snippet.
